title: Stop re-reading your notes
teaser: A week after studying, students who re-read remembered 40%. Students who tested themselves remembered 61%. A 20-second reel.

slides.alt: Frame from the reel: two bars showing that a week later, students who re-read a passage remembered 40% and students who tested themselves remembered 61%.

body: In one study, students who re-read a passage remembered 40% of it a week later. Students who tested themselves remembered 61%. And the re-readers felt more confident.
Close the book. Try to recall. Then check what you missed.
forDesigners: Swap a re-read for a quick recall prompt. It feels harder, and that's why it works.

sources.label: Roediger, H.L. & Karpicke, J.D. (2006). Test-enhanced learning: Taking memory tests improves long-term retention. Psychological Science, 17(3), 249–255. Experiment 2.
